subject: Request: bounded-availability exception for Hydra Labs private VPC edge latency
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@hydralabs.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference>
Cc: ops@hydralabs.com
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent edge latency — request for availability carveout

Tessa — thanks for taking this. Over the past 36 hours we've seen two spikes where requests from our EU users to the private VPC endpoints through our edge fabric spiked to 450–700ms additional tail latency. The traces point to packet drops/queueing at our carrier handoff (see attached pcap).

We're running Redwood Private inside our VPC with your edge egress pinned to our peering region. From our side it looks like the path instability is on our ISP/edge device chain, not Redwood's runtime. Given that Hydra controls the edge WAN and will be remediating with the carrier, we'd like to propose a bounded availability carveout in the SLA that excludes customer-managed edge-induced latency beyond the RTO/RPO your team owns. Practically: a clause acknowledging that latency above X ms attributable to customer-controlled network components won't count toward Redwood's latency credits, with a short audit/evidence process.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept that as an exception for private VPCs, and what evidence you require? We can provide packet captures, BGP logs, and our carrier incident report. Also happy to hop on a short call.

Attachments: hydra-network-trace-20280725.pcap (pcap), hydra-edge-topology-diagram.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Head of Platform — Hydra Labs
daniel.park@hydralabs.com
+1 (415) 555-0137
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@hydralabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 26 Jul 2028 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent edge latency — request for availability carveout

Thanks Daniel — sorry to hear about the impact. Looping in Karthik (contracts) and Vanessa (observability/CS) so we can scope an approach quickly.

Quick asks from our side to evaluate and draft language:
- Can you confirm timestamps for the two incidents and any correlating carrier tickets (ticket ids OK).
- Please attach the full PCAP and a short note on whether NAT or additional middleboxes are present between your edge and the peering.
- Do you have a proposed duration for the carveout (temporary during carrier remediation vs. permanent shared-resp appendix)?

A few notes on Redwood's side: we typically own runtime, compilation, and data-plane within the host boundary (the model runtime, KV cache, and our managed egress). We do not accept carveouts that absolve Redwood from runtime degradations. For edge-sourced latency we can accept a documented exclusion if it's clearly attributable to customer-controlled network components and there's an evidence workflow (PCAP/BGP dump + carrier ticket + a 72-hr reproducibility window).

Vanessa — could you run an initial correlation between our token latency traces and the timestamps Daniel sent? Karthik — once we have the evidence, can you draft a short shared-responsibility paragraph (1–2 sentences) we can propose for their contract?

If it's helpful, we can schedule a 30-min working session later this week to agree the evidence bar and the wording.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Customer Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@hydralabs.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference>
Cc: ops@hydralabs.com
Date: Thu, 27 Jul 2028 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent edge latency — request for availability carveout

Tessa — attaching the full PCAP and a short network timeline. Carrier ticket numbers: XY-12981 (07/24), XY-12995 (07/25). The topology doc shows an F5 load balancer and an explicit NAT at our edge; the peering handoff sits between our edge router and ISP ASN 61500.

Proposed draft sentence from Hydra legal for the SLA appendix (we're flexible on exact phrasing):
"Where customer-managed network elements (including but not limited to edge routers, third-party CDNs, and carrier handoffs) are the proximate cause of increased request latency to the Redwood Private control/egress plane beyond normal operational baselines, such latency shall be excluded from Redwood's latency SLO calculations pending proof of attribution submitted by customer. Proof of attribution shall include packet captures, BGP route dumps, and carrier trouble tickets; Redwood will have 72 hours to validate and either accept or reject the attribution."

Attachments: hydra-network-trace-20280725.pcap, hydra-edge-topology-diagram.pdf

Happy to join the working session.

—Daniel
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@hydralabs.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 28 Jul 2028 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed shared-responsibility language and monitoring requirements

Daniel / Tessa — thanks for the packet and timeline. I reviewed the PCAP and the carrier IDs; on the face of it the congestion appears to be upstream of Redwood's egress. Below is the contract language Redwood can accept as a one-paragraph appendix for Private/VPC deployments when the customer operates edge WAN components. Feel free to iterate.

Proposed clause (short form):
"Customer-managed network components that sit upstream of Redwood's designated peering point, and that are operated and maintained by the customer or the customer's carriers, are outside Redwood Inference's latency SLO obligations when attribution is validated per the Evidence Protocol below. Redwood retains responsibility for runtime availability, model-serving latency within the host network boundary, and any latency introduced by Redwood-managed egress."

Evidence Protocol (summary):
- Required artifacts: PCAP (server and client sides if available), BGP route dump, carrier trouble ticket(s), and a short remediation timeline.
- Validation window: Redwood will validate artifacts within 72 hours. Validation consists of correlating token-level latency traces from Redwood runtime with timestamps in the supplied artifacts and identifying consistent path-level increases on the customer-controlled segment.
- Temporary measures: If the customer provides credible evidence, Redwood may suspend latency credits for the affected windows. If evidence is inconclusive, Redwood and customer will execute a joint packet-capture session (60–90 minutes) during a mutually agreed window.

Operational asks before we sign:
1) A telemetry stream (s3/http) where Hydra can push edge latency histograms (1s granularity) for the validation window.
2) Admin contact for carrier escalation and a single legal POI for signoff on the appendix.
3) Agreed canary: we suggest a 14-day canary where Redwood will monitor and report but not apply credits while remediation occurs.

Credit calculation note: we cannot accept broad permanent carveouts. Credits are only excluded for windows where attribution is validated; the existing SLA credit table remains in force for all other windows.

If this tracks, I can produce a redline and a DocuSign envelope (I included a sample redline as redwood-shared-resp-draft-v1.docx). Also looping Vanessa to prototype the telemetry ingestion for the 72-hr validation.

—Karthik
VP, Legal & Contracts
Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@hydralabs.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 14:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent edge latency — request for availability carveout

Thanks everyone — this is very productive. Next steps we agreed on the 30-min working session:
- Hydra to provide final PCAP + BGP dump + carrier remediation ETA (if not already done) — Daniel
- Redwood to spin up a temporary telemetry sink (s3 bucket) and a joint capture window; Vanessa will send an ingestion URL and minimal schema by EOD tomorrow.
- Karthik to circulate DocuSign redline (DEAL-8472-HYDRA) with the short-form clause and the Evidence Protocol; customer to review and sign if acceptable.
- Canary: 14 days where we monitor but do not apply SLA credits unless attribution is validated.

Daniel — can you confirm the legal POI and carrier escalation POC so we can include them in the DocuSign and the JIRA SUP ticket? I'll open SUP-5921 and link it to the contract envelope. If all good, I'll also propose a tentative canary start date of 2028-08-02.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Customer Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference
